title: Parry–Romberg syndrome: a novel treatment algorithm derived from long-term follow-up and more than 40 years of surgeon’s experience
html: Parry–Romberg syndrome (PRS), or progressive hemifacial atrophy, is a rare, heterogeneous disorder characterized by unilateral facial atrophy affecting the skin, subcutaneous tissue, muscle, and sometimes osseocartilaginous structures. Due to its variability in severity and unclear treatment timing, a standardized surgical approach remains controversial. A retrospective review was conducted of patients diagnosed with PRS who were evaluated or treated by the senior author between 1978 and 2018. Inclusion criteria required availability of complete medical records and photographs.
